Supporting evidence: £592m Technologies dividends in Q1 2026, $165m capital injected into XTX Capital in Jan-Apr 2026, and capital reductions at XTX Markets Ltd and Trading Ltd in Jul 2026.

evidence.gaps:
There are no consolidated group accounts. XTX Holdings Ltd (Cayman) and its parents XTX Midco and XTX Topco (Cayman) explicitly do not consolidate. The FY2025 statement of the Cayman company XTX Holdings Ltd is solo and shows only dividends. So no single filing gives group-wide revenue, profit or headcount; every group figure here is my reconstruction from entity filings.

Missing entity data:
- P&L and headcount for the non-UK entities: XTX Markets SAS (Paris), XTX Markets Pte (Singapore), the India, Armenia and Finland/Norway data-centre entities, and XTX Holdings LLC.
- XTX Markets LLC publishes only a balance sheet. I derived its net income from retained earnings and dividends, so the 2021 figure assumes no dividend.
- The XTX Capital 2021-2023 and XTX Investments UK details were not extracted.

Headcount:
- No filing discloses group headcount.
- UK figures (Technologies, LLP, and before 2021 XTX Markets Ltd) are filed annual averages.
- Non-UK staff are inferred (about 0-10 in 2015-18, rising to about 90 in 2025), so error bars are wide (±10-25%).
- The year-end vs average distinction is unavailable for non-UK staff.

2026: no financial data. The latest hard datapoints are Technologies dividends of £331m (Jan) and £261m (Mar 2026), XTX Capital capital injections through Apr 2026, and the website headcount on 2026-10-08. The 2026 YTD revenue figure is a modeled estimate for 1 Jan-30 Sep 2026.

Sources I could not reach:
- The web-search budget ran out after the first query, so I could not systematically find FT, Bloomberg, Financial News, Times or Sunday Times coverage per year.
- FT and Bloomberg figures appear only second-hand, via Wikipedia and eFinancialCareers.
- The Wayback Machine was blocked and pappers.fr returned 403.
- No rating-agency reports, debt deals or LevFin coverage exist or were found; XTX appears to have no public debt.

FX: annual averages are from memory (GBP/USD: 2015 1.5285, 2016 1.3555, 2017 1.2886, 2018 1.3349, 2019 1.2767, 2020 1.2838, 2021 1.3757, 2022 1.2369, 2023 1.2435, 2024 1.2781, 2025 ~1.32). The orchestrator should re-check them.

Two caveats on early years: 2015 covers only H2 (advisory fees from GSA), and 2016 revenue is mostly fee income from GSA/GPT1 rather than direct trading P&L.
evidence.red_flags:
1) Press double-counting. Finance Magnates and eFinancialCareers report 'combined revenue' of £3.93bn (2025), £2.74bn (2024) and '~£2bn' (2023) by adding Technologies' net revenue to the trading entities' revenue.
- This counts twice the revenue the trading entities pass to Technologies (the UK group paid £829m to affiliates in 2025).
- It also leaves out the LLP research fee that Technologies nets out of its revenue (£1,734m in 2025).
- Economically consistent group revenue is about £5.0bn for 2025. The FT 2022 figure (£2.5bn revenue, £1.1bn profit, via Wikipedia) looks like the same summing method, and I could not verify it.

2) Misattribution. Finance Magnates (May 2022) says XTX Markets Technologies had revenue of £1.477bn (2021) and £1.065bn (2020).
- The filings show £903.5m and £412.8m.
- The press numbers equal Technologies + XTX Markets Ltd (+ Trading Ltd).
- The same article states XTX Markets Ltd revenue as '£531,558', which is in £'000.
- Finance Magnates (Aug 2021) labels the 2019 admin cost as 2020.

3) Intra-group entity figures are not group figures and must not be summed:
- Technologies' revenue is all intra-group service fees.
- The LLP's revenue is all fees from one affiliate (Technologies).
- XTX Markets Ltd's revenue fell from £652m (2020) to £62m (2025) because activity migrated to Trading Ltd and to non-UK affiliates, not because the business declined.

4) Headcount restatement. Technologies reported 133 average staff for 2022 in its 2022 accounts, then restated 2022 to 84 in the 2023 accounts, with identical wages (£37.16m). Its 2021 figure of 137 implies only about £198k of wages per head, so it is probably on the same broader basis. eFC conflates these ('137 employees back in 2022').

5) LLP member count. Average members for 2024 are 31 in the 2024 accounts but 26 in the 2025 accounts comparative. eFC's '£1.28bn ($1.35bn)' uses a wrong conversion (about $1.64bn).

6) Group headcount claims conflict:
- The website says '300 employees'; Wikipedia attributes that 300 to a 2024 source, so the website number may be stale or rounded.
- The FY2025 Modern Slavery statement says '200+ staff members or contractors'.
- Bloomberg, via eFC in 2025, says 'over 250'.

7) The UK trading entities report zero employees in their country-by-country tables (2023-2025). Revenue per head at entity level is therefore meaningless; staff sit in Technologies and the LLP (24 members plus 19 employees in 2025).

8) Presentation inconsistency in Technologies' accounts. Payments to affiliates for 2024 (£1,409m) include the LLP research cost, while the 2025 figure (£393m) excludes it. The jump in non-LLP affiliate payments, from £128m to £393m, is unexplained (possibly data centres or overseas staff).

9) Non-trading gains to exclude:
- XTX Investments booked £217m of venture mark-to-market gains in 2025.
- XTX Holdings Ltd booked a £92m credit in administrative expenses in 2025, likely gains on its gold holdings (£332m), plus interest income.

10) Ownership: Finance Magnates says Gerko owns about 75%, while the 2018-2021 accounts say the directors indirectly control 83-84%. The ultimate controlling party is consistently Alex Gerko.

11) Profit definition matters. LLP partner profit shares (£1.73bn in 2025) are economically partner compensation. Group pre-tax profit is about £4.3bn including them and about £2.6bn excluding them.
evidence.summary:
XTX publishes no group accounts. I rebuilt group net trading revenue from primary filings on Companies House and SEC EDGAR, all downloaded and read (most OCR'd from scans).

Entities used:
- XTX Markets Ltd, the main trading entity until 2020.
- XTX Markets Technologies Ltd, the IP and service company that has employed the UK staff since 2020. It collects profit-split fees from all trading entities, net of research fees paid to XTX Research LLP.
- XTX Research LLP, the partners' vehicle, whose only client is an affiliate.
- XTX Holdings (UK) Ltd consolidated, covering XTX Markets Ltd and XTX Markets Trading Ltd.
- XTX Markets LLC (US), XTX Capital and XTX Holdings Ltd (Cayman).

Method: for 2020 onwards, group revenue = Technologies' gross service fee + revenue retained by UK trading entities + LLC and other non-UK retained profit and costs. I cross-checked this against the sum of entity pre-tax profits plus external costs; the gap between the two methods forms the error bar.

2026 YTD, modeled for 1 Jan-30 Sep 2026: about £3.75bn [2.6-5.0], roughly $5.0bn [3.5-6.7]. Headcount is about 290 [260-320]; the website showed 300 on 2026-10-08. No 2026 financials have been filed; the latest hard data is £592m of Technologies dividends paid in Jan-Mar 2026.

Group pre-tax profit including LLP partner profit, GBP m:
- 2015: ~65 | 2016: ~104 | 2017: ~106 | 2018: ~220 | 2019: ~311
- 2020: ~1,051 | 2021: ~1,511 | 2022: ~2,280 | 2023: ~1,984 | 2024: ~3,309 | 2025: ~4,293 (about $5.7bn)

Excluding the LLP partner pool, 2025 pre-tax profit is about £2.57bn.

Headcount basis: UK staff come from filed averages (XTX Markets Ltd before 2020, then Technologies, plus LLP employees and individual members). Non-UK staff are inferred, and the band is bounded by the FY2025 Modern Slavery statement ('200+ staff members or contractors'), Bloomberg's 'over 250' and the website's '300 employees'.

Reliability: entity figures are high. Group figures are medium, about ±3-7% on revenue for 2020+ and ±10-25% on headcount. Treat the widely repeated press totals (£3.93bn for 2025, £2.74bn for 2024) as double-counted and do not use them.
